'''Philip Michael Tuts''' is an [[Americans|American]] high-energy experimental [[particle physics|particle physicist]], and Professor and Chair of the [[Columbia University Physics Department]].<ref name=profile>{{cite web|title=Philip Michael Tuts Faculty Profile|url=http://physics.columbia.edu/people/profile/436|website=Columbia University Physics Department|accessdate=26 January 2015}}</ref> Tuts is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=wlf>{{cite web|title=Michael Tuts|url=http://www.worldleaders.columbia.edu/participants/michael-tuts|website=World Leaders Forum|accessdate=26 January 2015}}</ref> He holds a seat on the executive committees of the United States LHC Users' Association and the [[American Physics Society]] Forum on Physics and Society, and is Divisional Councilor of the Division of Particles and Fields of APS.<ref name=usluo>{{cite web|last1=Tuts|first1=Michael|title=USLUO Statement|url=https://www.usluo.org/USLUO-tuts2013.pdf|website=USLUO|accessdate=26 January 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150128131954/https://www.usluo.org/USLUO-tuts2013.pdf|archivedate=28 January 2015}}</ref> Tuts earned his Bachelor's in Physics from [[MIT]] in 1974, and his MA and PhD from the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]] in 1976 and 1979, respectively.<ref name="profile" /> He joined the physics department at Columbia University in the City of New York in 1983 and was appointed Chair in 2014.<ref name="profile" /><ref name="wlf" /> Tuts is currently a member of the [[ATLAS experiment]] team at [[CERN]] and formerly served as US ATLAS Operations Program Manager.<ref name=uslhc>{{cite web|title=Columbia University|url=http://www.uslhc.us/The_US_and_the_LHC/Collaborating_Institutions/Columbia_University|website=United States at the Large Hadron Collider|accessdate=26 January 2015}}</ref>

As operations manager, he led the team of 400 American physicists working on ATLAS during the experiment that led to the discovery of the [[Higgs boson]].<ref name=freeman>{{cite news|last1=Freeman|first1=David|title=Scientists Raise Doubts About Higgs Boson Discovery, Say It Could Be Another Particle|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/11/10/higgs-boson-discovery-particle_n_6133502.html|accessdate=26 January 2015|work=Huffington Post}}</ref><ref name=craig>{{cite news|last1=Craig|first1=David|title=Mike Tuts is among 20 Columbia physicists chasing God's particle|url=http://magazine.columbia.edu/explorations/winter-2009-10/physicists-gods-particle?page=0,1|accessdate=26 January 2015|work=Columbia Magazine}}</ref> Tuts is project manager of the [[D0 experiment]] at Fermilab and also leads the Calorimeter subgroup.<ref name="profile" />

Tuts has also used the [[CUSB]] detector at the [[Cornell Electron Storage Ring]] to investigate the [[Upsilon meson]].<ref name="profile" /> Tuts has authored over 600 publications in Physics.<ref name="wlf" /> He believes in the importance of public outreach by prominent physicists and the science community,<ref name=raymond>{{cite news|last1=Raymond|first1=Joan|title=I'm a Particle Physicist. Want to Chat?|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/07/14/business/14flier.html?_r=0|accessdate=26 January 2015|work=New York Times|date=July 13, 2009}}</ref> and writes a blog for the [[Huffington Post]].<ref name=huffpo>{{cite news|last1=Tuts|first1=Michael|title=Blog of Michael Tuts|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/michael-tuts/|accessdate=26 January 2015|work=Huffington Post}}</ref> Professor Tuts has also given talks about his work at amateur societies and for lay audiences, and organized a gathering to watch the Higgs Boson announcement at Columbia University at 3 a.m. ET (9a.m. Geneva time).<ref name=than>{{cite news|last1=Than|first1=Ker|title="God Particle" Found? "Historic Milestone" From Higgs Boson Hunters|url=http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2012/07/120704-god-particle-higgs-boson-new-cern-science/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120705142109/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2012/07/120704-god-particle-higgs-boson-new-cern-science/|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 5, 2012|accessdate=26 January 2015|work=National Geographic|date=July 4, 2012}}</ref> At Columbia, he teaches introductory undergraduate mechanics and electromagnetics courses, which he enjoys. In 2004, Tuts was awarded a Presidential Award for Outstanding Teaching.<ref name="wlf" /> He has stated that he has been mistaken for [[Stephen King]] on several occasions.<ref name="raymond" />

== Selected publications ==
*"Observation of the {{Subatomic particle|Upsilon}}´´´ at the Cornell Electron Storage Ring", with CUSB Collaboration, ''Phys. Rev. Lett.'' 45, 222 (1980).
*"Observation of P-Wave {{Subatomic particle|B}}{{Subatomic particle|AntiB}} Bound States", with CUSB Collaboration, ''Phys. Rev. Lett.'' 49, 1612 (1984)
*"Measurement of the Upsilon Mass", with W. W. Mackay et al. and the CUSB collaboration, ''Phys. Rev. Lett.'' 55, 36 (1985).
*"CUSB-II a high precision electromagnetic spectrometer", with CUSB Collaboration, ''Nucl. Instrum. Methods A''A309, 450 (1991)
*"Observation of the Top Quark, with the D0 Collaboration", ''Phys. Rev. Lett.''. 74, 2632 (1995)
*"Limits on the ZZg and Zgg couplings in pbarp Collisions at S1/2 = 1.8 TeV", with the D0 Collaboration, ''Phys. Rev. Lett.'' 75, 1028 (1995)
*"Search for Large Extra Dimensions in Dielectron and Diphoton production", ''Phys. Rev. Lett.'' {86} 1156 (2001)
*"Search for Leptoquark Pairs Decaying to nunu+Jets in pbarp Collisions at sqrt(s)=1.8 TeV", ''Phys. Rev. Lett.'' {88}, 191801 (2002)
